title: stats-check (real-replay-path byte-identity pin) is a manual verb, not wired into the harness suite or CI
evidence:
harness/main.odin:67:	if verb == "stats-check" {
		if len(rest) != 1 {
			usage()
		}
...
		code := stats_check(rest[0], &cat)
.github/workflows/ci.yml:
 70:        run: odin test core
 83:        run: tools/harness.sh run
 89:        run: tools/harness.sh drift-check
 97:        run: tools/harness.sh preview-check
detail: AC1 asks the byte-identity be 'pinned by test'. Core unit pins run in CI, but a future asymmetry between run_demo and replay_hashes stats emission (e.g. emitting on paused ticks) would pass odin test core, harness run, and CI undetected.
recommended_fix: Add a CI step (and/or a line in tools/harness.sh's run path) invoking stats-check on at least qos_contention and pause, next to drift-check/preview-check.

title: Committed spec leaves the AC5 full-suite task unchecked while the PR body claims the suite green
evidence:
spec-5-7-runtime-telemetry.md:109:- [ ] Full suite: `odin test core` + harness build (shadow ODIN_ROOT) + `harness run` all green, goldens byte-identical -- AC5.
_pr_body.md:103:- `harness run` — 25/25 demos green; goldens BYTE-identical (AC4).
detail: Contradictory state between the in-PR spec (task open) and the PR body (suite verified green). Reviewers cannot tell whether the golden run actually executed before the PR opened.
recommended_fix: Tick the spec checkbox after running the suite (or note the PR-body claim supersedes it); keep one authoritative verification record.

title: App silently disables the stats stream when --stats-out lacks a path token; spec matrix says usage error
detail: A trailing `--stats-out` with no path silently turns telemetry off — the user believes the stream is being written. The harness errors; the app never surfaces the malformed flag.
recommended_fix: On seeing --stats-out without a following token, eprintf a usage error and exit 1 before InitWindow, mirroring the harness behavior.
